p.scope-of-this-document: **Scope of this document.** The reference directory layout for an addressable spec tree, the PROP / FEAT distinction, the decision table for where each kind of fact lives, and the `.human/` private buffer with its physical-invisibility rule.

p.protocol-document-pointer: The addressing scheme the layout serves is defined in [`ADDRESSABLE-SPECS-PROTOCOL.xml`](ADDRESSABLE-SPECS-PROTOCOL.xml).

tree.title: The reference tree
tree.fence: project/ ├── spec/ # the IPC buffer (shared state) │ ├── BOOT.md # entry point — the agent reads this first │ ├── WAL.md # continuation state between sessions │ ├── SPEC-PROTOCOL.md # how specs are updated (conflict rules) │ ├── common/ │ │ ├── PROP-000.xml # foundational decisions │ │ └── structure.md # module map │ └── modules/ │ ├── payments/ │ │ ├── PROP-001.xml # standing decisions for this module │ │ └── FEAT-001.md # one feature slice │ └── client/ ├── src/ # artifacts — generated, verifiable, re-creatable ├── tests/ # executable specs ├── .human/ # human-only buffer, excluded from agent view │ └── shortcuts.md # copy-paste corrections, private notes ├── .<agent>ignore # what the agent never sees (.human/ at minimum) └── CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / … # harness entry files redirecting to spec/BOOT.md

p.SPEC-OR-SPECS-PICK-ONE: `spec/` or `specs/` — either; pick one and never mix.

p.three-zones-lead: The tree divides into three zones with different loss semantics:

facts.ZONE-SHARED-STATE: **shared state** (`spec/` — losing it is a catastrophe, it is the only channel between the two processes),
facts.ZONE-ARTIFACTS: **artifacts** (`src/`, `tests/` — losing a file is an inconvenience; it can be regenerated from the spec),
facts.ZONE-PRIVATE-BUFFERS: and **private buffers** (`.human/` — one process's memory, invisible to the other).

p.HARNESS-ENTRY-FILES-ARE-THIN-REDIRECTS: Harness entry files (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, and whatever the next tool demands) should be thin redirects into `spec/BOOT.md`.

p.one-boot-sequence-many-doors: One boot sequence, many doors — the alternative is N slowly diverging copies.

p.PROP-IS-THE-LAW-FEAT-IS-A-PROJECT-UNDER-: PROP is the law; FEAT is a project under that law.

p.A-LASTING-DECISION-MOVES-UP-INTO-A-PROP: When a FEAT uncovers a lasting decision, the decision moves *up* into a PROP and the FEAT cites it — the slice document never becomes the permanent home of a permanent rule.

p.NUMBER-PER-MODULE-AND-NEVER-RENUMBER: Number per module (`PROP-001`, `FEAT-003`, …) and never renumber: the number is part of the URI, and URIs are forever ([authoring rules §anchor-stability](authoring-rules.xml#anchor-stability)).

td.ROW-HOME-FEATURE-SCOPE: A feature's scope and acceptance criteria

td.fact: `spec/modules/<m>/FEAT-*` — or a campaign plan where the project runs slices as plans (`flow:campaign-plans`)

td.ROW-HOME-NEXT-SESSION-STEP: What the next session must do first

td.ROW-HOME-SPEC-PROTOCOL: How specs are updated, conflict rules

td.fact: protocol docs at the spec root
code and doc comments — never the spec

p.CHOOSING-BETWEEN-THE-TWO-HOMES: **Choosing between the two homes.** The row above names two carriers for a feature's plan; which one carries it is a choice with consequences, because it decides whether the plan stays addressable after the work ships and whether it outlives the effort that produced it. Make the choice explicitly and say it to whoever asked for the work.

p.A-FEATURE-DOCUMENT-CARRIES-A-FEATURE: A **feature document** carries work that is a feature: it has a name its user would recognise, it will be referred to again after it ships, and it will not finish in one sitting. It is one file in the feature's home, and it is addressable like any other specification document — every anchored heading it carries becomes an address for free, with nothing to register.

p.A-CAMPAIGN-PLAN-CARRIES-A-PROGRAMME: A **campaign plan** carries a programme rather than a feature: many documents or many packages, a unit of work that is a batch rather than a change, and a lifetime that ends when the campaign closes. Its zone is disposable by design, so nothing that must outlive the campaign belongs inside it.

p.NEITHER-CARRIES-SMALL-WORK: **Neither carries small work.** A three-line change planned into a feature document is a document with more ceremony than content; the current slice's checklist carries it, and that is the whole plan it needs.

p.THE-THRESHOLD-STAYS-QUALITATIVE: The threshold between them stays qualitative on purpose. A line count would be a number nobody measured, and a rule that files work by size rather than by kind puts a rename and a subsystem in one bucket whenever the count happens to agree.

p.THE-CHOICE-BELONGS-TO-WHOEVER-ASKED-FOR-: **The choice belongs to whoever asked for the work, not to the agent doing it.** An agent that picks the carrier silently has decided how long the work stays findable, which is not a decision it was given: it proposes a carrier with its reason, and asks.

p.DEFAULT-A-HOMELESS-FACT-INTO-THE-SPEC-TR: When a fact has no obvious home, default it into the spec tree rather than a wiki, a gist, or a head: a teammate — human or agent — who clones the repository must receive everything the project knows.

p.HUMAN-BUFFER-HOLDS-TEXT-THE-AGENT-MUST-N: `.human/` holds text that must never enter the agent's context: copy-paste correction snippets ("you are drifting, re-read the spec"), negotiation notes, half-formed doubts.

p.two-reasons-lead: Two reasons to keep it out:

facts.REASON-TOKEN-COST: **Token cost.** Every file the agent reads is context spent; a shortcuts file is pure overhead for any task.
facts.REASON-REACTION-RISK: **Reaction risk.** An agent that reads "you are drifting" mid-task may *respond* to it — reflecting on drift it has not committed, polluting the session with a correction nobody issued.

p.PHYSICAL-INVISIBILITY-BEATS-LOGICAL-PROH: The enforcement rule: **physical invisibility beats logical prohibition.**

p.DO-NOT-WRITE-A-NEVER-READ-LINE-IN-THE-BO: Do not write "never read `.human/`" in the boot file — that line itself costs tokens forever and invites the very attention it forbids.

p.LIST-THE-BUFFER-IN-THE-IGNORE-MECHANISM: Instead, list `.human/` in the agent's ignore mechanism (`.claudeignore`, `.aiexclude`, `.cursorignore` — whatever the harness supports), so the directory does not exist as far as the agent can see.

p.a-firewall-beats-a-no-entry-sign: A firewall beats a "no entry" sign.

p.NO-IGNORE-FILE-MEANS-KEEP-IT-OUTSIDE-THE: If the harness supports no ignore file, keep the buffer outside the repository working tree entirely.

p.layout-is-the-uri-scheme-lead: The layout is the URI scheme made physical:

facts.SEGMENT-MODULE-IS-THE-DIRECTORY: the directory name under `spec/modules/` is the `<module>` segment;
facts.SEGMENT-DOC-IS-THE-FILE-NAME: the file name minus `.md` is the `<doc>` segment;
facts.SEGMENT-FRAGMENT-IS-THE-ANCHOR: the `{#anchor}` in the file is the fragment.

p.A-URI-RESOLVES-WITH-ZERO-INDEX: `spec://com.example.shop/PROP-001#verification.timeout` resolves with zero index: `spec/modules/com.example.shop/PROP-001.md`, then find `{#verification.timeout}`.

p.KEEP-THE-MAPPING-ONE-TO-ONE: Keep the mapping one-to-one — the moment resolution needs a lookup table, every citation costs a search, and the twenty-token correction stops being twenty tokens.

p.REVERSE-DNS-WHEN-SPECS-MAY-BE-SHARED: Use reverse-DNS module directory names when the specs could ever be shared beyond this repository; short local names are fine when they provably cannot.

migrating.title: Migrating an existing project

p.decisions-arrive-scattered: Most projects arrive with decisions scattered across READMEs, wikis, docstrings, and heads.

migrating.fence: Inventory every Markdown file in this repository that states a decision, requirement, or plan. For each: current path, what kind of fact it holds (per the what-goes-where table in spec/flows/addressable-specs/spec-tree-layout.xml), its proposed home in the spec tree, and which headings need {#anchor}s. Output a migration table. Move nothing yet.

p.MIGRATE-IN-SMALL-REVIEWABLE-STEPS: Review the table, then migrate in small, reviewable steps — the tree is load-bearing, so it deserves the same care as a schema migration.

facts.SUM-THREE-ZONES: Three zones: shared state (`spec/`), artifacts (`src/`, `tests/`), private buffers (`.human/`). Their loss semantics differ; treat them accordingly.
facts.SUM-PROP-IS-LAW-FEAT-IS-A-SLICE: PROP is standing law, FEAT is a slice under it; lasting decisions migrate up. Numbers are part of URIs — never renumber.
facts.SUM-EVERY-FACT-HAS-A-DESIGNATED-HOME: Every fact has a designated home; when in doubt, it goes into the spec tree, where a fresh clone can find it.
facts.SUM-HUMAN-BUFFER-IS-ENFORCED-BY-INVISIBI: `.human/` is enforced by ignore-file invisibility, not by a rule the agent must read to obey.
facts.SUM-NAMES-ARE-THE-URI-SEGMENTS: Directory and file names *are* the URI segments — resolution must work with zero index.
